newsitem.title: CANADA: BASEBALL-HENTGEN WINS 20TH, ANDERSON HITS 50TH HOMER.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-HENTGEN WINS 20TH, ANDERSON HITS 50TH HOMER.

text.p: On the final day of the regular season, Pat Hentgen staked an oustside claim to the Cy Young Award with his 20th win as the Toronto Blue Jays beat the playoff-bound Baltimore Orioles 4-1 Sunday.
Hentgen (20-10, 3.22 ERA) established a career high for wins and joined the Yankees' Andy Pettite as the only A.L. pitchers with 20.
He allowed one run -- Brady Anderson's record-setting 50th homer -- and seven hits in 7 1/3 innings.
But he will have a tough time outpolling Pettitte, who won 21 games with a 3.87 ERA and anchored the injury-riddled staff of the American League East champion Yankees.
"The season's over," Hentgen said. "The Cy is out of my hands. If it happens, it happens. I think they're gonna look at the numbers and the numbers don't lie."
For the 12th time this season, Anderson led off the game with a homer, breaking the major-league record set by Bobby Bonds of San Francisco in 1973.

It also was his 50th homer, breaking the club record set by Frank Robinson in 1966. Anderson became the 14th player in major-league history to hit 50 homers in a season -- and second this year, along with Oakland's Mark McGwire, who wound up with 52.
Anderson is more proud of reaching 50 homers than the leadoff record, but he'll take it.
"That's something that's sort of strange," he said. "It doesn't mean as much to me as the 50, but anytime you have a major-league record, it's nice."
Baltimore (88-74), which spent the first half of the season bumbling and bickering, went 37-22 after July 28 to claim the wild-card berth and will face the Indians in the first round of the playoffs.

"Up until a day ago, I wasn't thinking about it," shortstop Cal Ripken said. "They have a balanced team and one of the best pitching staffs in the league. I think we match up OK. If we pitch well, we'll have a decent chance."
The Blue Jays (74-88) have finished under .500 for three straight seasons after winning consecutive World Series in 1992-93.
In Kansas City, Tim Belcher allowed one run over 8 1/3 innings and Joe Randa homered and drove in two runs as the Royals denied the Cleveland Indians their 100th win, 4-1.
Belcher (15-11) scattered eight hits, walked none and struck out three to tie a career high in wins.
Kansas City finished last in the A.L. League Central at 75-86, the first time in team history the Royals have ended up in the basement.
Cleveland, which won its second straight A.L. Central, finished 99-62, falling short of becoming the first team since the 1979-80 Orioles to post back-to-back 100-win seasons.
In Boston, Reggie Jefferson's one-out single in the bottom of the ninth scored Darren Bragg and gave the Red Sox a 6-5 victory over the New York Yankees.

A.L. Rookie of the Year favourite Derek Jeter hit his 10th homer for the Yankees (92-70), who won the A.L. East and face Texas in the first round of the playoffs. Jeter boosted his RBI total to 78, the most by a Yankees shortstop since Frank Crosetti in 1936.

"Texas has seemed to wear out lefties all year," Yankees ace David Cone said. "I think they've got enough balance to wear out anybody. Our key is going to be to try to get enough quality starting pitching, get a lead and turn it over to our bullpen."
At Texas, Kevin Elster completed a phenomenal comeback season by cracking a go-ahead two-run homer in the sixth that lifted the Rangers past the California Angels 4-3.
The Rangers, who won the A.L. West for their first-ever post-season appearance, secured their second 90-win season in team history.
Elster, seemingly done in by shoulder injuries, ended the season hitting .252 with a surprising 24 homers and 99 RBI.

The slick-fielding shortstop provided solid defence up the middle all season and unmatched production from the bottom of the batting order. He was signed with an outside shot to make the team but became the starter when Benji Gil was hurt.
At Minnesota, Paul Molitor capped a magical season with an RBI single in the bottom of the 10th that lifted the Twins to a 5-4 victory over the Chicago White Sox.
The 40-year-old Molitor, who earlier this month collected his 3,000th hit, stroked his third hit of the game, boosting his season total to 228, most in the major leagues.

In Detroit, Matt Mieske's two-run single in the top of the 10th gave the Milwaukee Brewers a 7-5 victory over the Tigers, who finished the season with a club-record 17 straight home losses and the worst record in baseball in 27 years.
Detroit finished 52-110, the worst since expansion San Diego went 52-110 in 1969.
In Oakland, Geronimo Berroa had a sacrifice fly in a two-run third inning as the Athletics trimmed the Seattle Mariners 3-1 in the shortest game this season for both teams.
The game lasted just two hours as both teams played out the season.
Seattle star Ken Griffey Jr, batting leadoff to get extra at-bats, went 0-for-4 in his bid for his 50th homer.
